Splice-Site Strength from the Annotation and the Genome

Source: R/splice-sites.R
splice_sites.Rd

Scores the donor (5') and acceptor (3') splice site of every intron with position weight matrices built from the annotation itself, and reports the weakest site of every transcript. A weak site is one way for an isoform to be rare or to be a splicing error; the score is evidence to read next to transcript_productivity(), not a classifier.

  • extract_splice_sites(x, genome_fasta) cuts the sequences around the splice sites out of a genome FASTA and stores them in the annotation directory. extract_transcript_sequences() does the same when it is given a genome FASTA, so this is only needed for directories whose sequences came from a transcript FASTA.

  • splice_site_strength(x) returns one row per transcript, or one row per intron with by = "intron".

Usage

extract_splice_sites(x, genome_fasta, overwrite = FALSE, chunk_bytes = 6.4e+07)

has_splice_sites(x)

splice_site_strength(
  self,
  gene_name = NULL,
  by = c("transcript", "intron"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An annotation directory path or an IsoformicExperiment.

genome_fasta

Path to a genome FASTA file (.fa, .fa.gz).

overwrite

Logical, replace an existing table (default FALSE).

chunk_bytes

Number of bytes read per chunk while streaming.

self

An annotation directory path or an IsoformicExperiment. An experiment reports its own transcripts.

gene_name

Optional gene names or IDs to keep.

by

"transcript" (default) or "intron".

...

Unused.

Value

  • extract_splice_sites(): the path of the written Parquet file, invisibly. The table has seqid, strand, intron_start, intron_end (1-based, inclusive), donor_seq and acceptor_seq.

  • splice_site_strength(): a tibble. By transcript: transcript_id, gene_id, gene_name, n_introns, n_scored, weakest_donor, weakest_acceptor, mean_donor, mean_acceptor and n_noncanonical; transcripts without introns have NA scores. By intron: one row per transcript and intron with the coordinates, the two window sequences, donor_score, acceptor_score and canonical_dinucleotides.

Details

The donor window holds the last 3 exonic and the first 6 intronic bases, the acceptor window the last 20 intronic and the first 3 exonic bases, in the direction of transcription (the windows of MaxEntScan, Yeo and Burge 2004). The matrices are trained on the unique introns of the canonical transcripts (is_canonical, see prepare_isoformic_annotation()), or on all introns when the annotation marks fewer than 100 canonical introns. A score is the sum over the window of log2(frequency / background), with the background taken from the base composition of the training windows and half a pseudocount per base. Positive means closer to the consensus.

Limits. The matrices assume that positions are independent, so they are weaker than MaxEntScan or a sequence model, and they describe the major (GT-AG) spliceosome: U12 introns and other non-canonical sites get low scores whatever their real efficiency (n_noncanonical counts the introns that are not GT-AG). Canonical transcripts train the matrices, so their own scores are slightly optimistic. Windows that run off the sequence or hold a base other than A, C, G or T are not scored.

References

Yeo, G., Burge, C.B. (2004). Maximum entropy modeling of short sequence motifs with applications to RNA splicing signals. Journal of Computational Biology 11(2-3), 377-394.

See also

extract_transcript_sequences(), transcript_productivity()

Examples

gff <- system.file("extdata", "example.gff3", package = "isoformic")
annot <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(
  gff,
  output_path = tempdir(),
  annot_name = "splice_demo"
)
#> ℹ Parsing example.gff3 (GFF) into /tmp/RtmpatoNKq/splice_demo.
has_splice_sites(annot)
#> [1] FALSE
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
genome <- download_reference(file_type = "genome_fasta", region = "primary")
extract_splice_sites(annot, genome_fasta = genome)
splice_site_strength(annot)
} # }
